slides.title: 5 lawn and yard myths that quietly hurt your grass and trees

slides.myth: Cut the grass short so you can mow less often.
slides.fact: Extension guides say never take off more than about a third of the blade in one mowing. Cutting too short stresses the lawn. For tall fescue, that means keeping it around 3 to 4 inches.
slides.source: University of Maryland and University of Georgia Extension

slides.myth: Leaving grass clippings on the lawn causes thatch.
slides.fact: It doesn't. Extension guides say clippings break down and return nutrients to the soil. Thatch builds up from other things, and a thick layer can actually keep clippings from reaching the soil.

slides.myth: A little water every day keeps a lawn healthy.
slides.fact: Frequent light watering encourages shallow roots. Wisconsin Extension says lawns need about 1 inch a week, from rain or sprinklers, and watering more often than once a week keeps roots shallow.

slides.myth: You have to rake every fall leaf off the lawn.
slides.fact: Mowing leaves into small pieces works too. A thick, wet mat of whole leaves is what smothers grass, but a light layer is fine. Michigan State research found mulching leaves helped the lawn.
slides.source: University of Minnesota and Michigan State University Extension

slides.myth: Piling mulch high around a tree is good for it.
slides.fact: A mulch volcano holds moisture against the bark. Extension guides say 2 to 4 inches is plenty, and it should be spread wide and kept from touching the trunk.
slides.source: University of Vermont, University of Illinois and University of Kentucky Extension
